title: Truth scenarios
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Spring 2: Hadith, akhlaq and Important Lessons
source: Written for islamic-studies/y8 lesson 12 (Pupil PDF worksheet: truth scenarios)
intro: Lesson 12: Akhlaq: truthfulness (sidq). Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

passage.title: Bukhari and Muslim
paras: Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise ... Lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire.

panels.title: Be with the truthful
points: 'O you who believe, fear Allah and be with the truthful' (9:119)
Truth in words, promises and work

head: Scenario
The truthful response
What it costs
What it gains
rows: You broke a vase at home
A friend sends you the answers to an online quiz

questions.q: Explain why truthfulness is described as a road to Paradise.
questions.a: Truth leads to righteousness and righteousness to Paradise (Bukhari and Muslim): one truth builds a good character.

questions.q: Which ayah says 'be with the truthful'?

Scenarios on the pupil PDF: a broken vase, an online quiz answer from a friend, a late homework excuse. For each, write the truthful response and what it costs and gains. Then a reflection in the portal response box: 'Being truthful is hardest when ... but ...'
questions.a: Truthful responses with honest costs and gains; reflection

questions.q: Extend: what is truthfulness in actions, not only words?
questions.a: Doing what you say; honest work; keeping promises.

questions.q: Stretch: why does lying become easier the more you do it?
questions.a: The heart gets used to it; the hadith says a person keeps lying until written as a liar.

questions.q: According to the hadith, lying leads to ...
questions.a: A) Wickedness. Lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness to the Fire (Bukhari and Muslim).

questions.q: Think again: is a small lie harmless?
questions.a: No: it starts a road to wickedness; truth builds good.
